display_title: 20-1-3 压力如何影响我们的判断

sentences.en: Some of the most important decisions of our lives occur while we’re feeling stressed and anxious.
sentences.zh: 人生中一些最重要的决定，是在我们感到紧张和焦虑时作出的。

sentences.en: From medical decisions to financial and professional ones, we are all sometimes required to weigh up information under stressful conditions.
sentences.zh: 无论是医疗、财务还是职业方面的决定，我们有时都需要在压力之下权衡各种信息。

sentences.en: But do we become better or worse at processing and using information under such circumstances?
sentences.zh: 可在这样的情形下，我们处理和运用信息的能力是变强了，还是变弱了？

sentences.en: My colleague and I, both neuroscientists, wanted to investigate how the mind operates under stress, so we visited some local fire stations.
sentences.zh: 我和同事都是神经科学家。我们想研究人的思维在压力下是如何运作的，于是走访了当地几座消防站。

sentences.en: Firefighters’ workdays vary quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 消防员每天的工作状况差别很大。

sentences.en: Some are pretty relaxed; they’ll spend their time washing the truck, cleaning equipment, cooking meals and reading.
sentences.zh: 有些日子很轻松，他们会洗消防车、清洁设备、做饭、读书。

sentences.en: Other days can be hectic, with numerous life-threatening incidents to attend to; they’ll enter burning homes to rescue trapped residents, and assist with medical emergencies.
sentences.zh: 另一些日子则可能忙得不可开交，有许多危及生命的突发事件要处理。他们要进入起火的住宅营救被困居民，还要协助应对紧急医疗情况。

sentences.en: These ups and downs presented the perfect setting for an experiment on how people’s ability to use information changes when they feel under pressure.
sentences.zh: 这种时忙时闲的工作状态提供了理想的实验环境，可以用来研究人在感到压力时，运用信息的能力会怎样变化。

sentences.en: We found that perceived threat acted as a trigger for a stress reaction that made the task of processing information easier for the firefighters – but only as long as it conveyed bad news.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，感知到的威胁会触发应激反应，使消防员更容易处理信息，但前提是这些信息传递的是坏消息。

sentences.en: This is how we arrived at these results.
sentences.zh: 我们是这样得出这些结果的。

sentences.en: We asked the firefighters to estimate their likelihood of experiencing 40 different adverse events in their life, such as being involved in an accident or becoming a victim of card fraud.
sentences.zh: 我们请消防员估计，一生中遭遇40种不同不利事件的可能性分别有多大，例如卷入事故，或成为银行卡诈骗的受害者。

sentences.en: We then gave them either good news (that their likelihood of experiencing these events was lower than they’d thought) or bad news (that it was higher) and asked them to provide new estimates.
sentences.zh: 随后，我们给他们好消息，也就是这些事发生在他们身上的可能性低于他们之前的估计，或者给他们坏消息，也就是可能性更高，再请他们重新估计。

sentences.en: People are normally quite optimistic – they will ignore bad news and embrace the good.
sentences.zh: 人们通常相当乐观，往往会忽视坏消息，欣然接受好消息。

sentences.en: This is what happened when the firefighters were relaxed; but when they were under stress, a different pattern emerged.
sentences.zh: 消防员处于放松状态时，情况正是如此。但当他们承受压力时，却出现了另一种模式。

sentences.en: Under these conditions, they became hyper-vigilant to bad news, even when it had nothing to do with their job (such as learning that the likelihood of card fraud was higher than they’d thought), and altered their beliefs in response.
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下，他们对坏消息变得格外警觉，哪怕这些消息与工作毫无关系，比如得知自己遭遇银行卡诈骗的可能性高于预期，他们也会相应地改变原先的看法。

sentences.en: In contrast, stress didn’t change how they responded to good news (such as learning that the likelihood of card fraud was lower than they’d thought).
sentences.zh: 相比之下，压力并没有改变他们对好消息的反应，例如得知自己遭遇银行卡诈骗的可能性比原先想的低。

sentences.en: Back in our lab, we observed the same pattern in students who were told they had to give a surprise public speech, which would be judged by a panel, recorded and posted online.
sentences.zh: 回到实验室后，我们在学生身上也观察到了同样的现象。这些学生被临时告知要当众演讲，演讲将由评审小组评判，还会被录下来并发布到网上。

sentences.en: Sure enough, their cortisol levels spiked, their heart rates went up and they suddenly became better at processing unrelated, yet alarming, information about rates of disease and violence.
sentences.zh: 果然，他们的皮质醇水平骤升，心率加快。他们突然更善于处理有关疾病和暴力事件发生率的信息，这些信息与眼前的事无关，却令人担忧。

sentences.en: When we experience stressful events, a physiological change is triggered that causes us to take in warnings and focus on what might go wrong.
sentences.zh: 当我们遇到压力事件时，身体会发生一种生理变化，使我们留意警示，专注于那些可能出问题的事。

sentences.en: Brain imaging reveals that this ‘switch’ is related to a sudden boost in a neural signal important for learning, specifically in response to unexpected warning signs, such as faces expressing fear.
sentences.zh: 脑成像显示，这种“切换”与一种对学习很重要的神经信号突然增强有关。具体来说，面对出乎意料的警示，比如看到一张流露出恐惧的脸时，就会出现这种反应。

sentences.en: Such neural engineering could have helped prehistoric humans to survive.
sentences.zh: 这样的神经机制或许曾帮助史前人类生存下来。

sentences.en: When our ancestors found themselves surrounded by hungry animals, they would have benefited from an increased ability to learn about hazards.
sentences.zh: 当我们的祖先发现自己被饥饿的动物包围时，更善于获取有关危险的信息，想必对他们有所帮助。

sentences.en: In a safe environment, however, it would have been wasteful to be on high alert constantly.
sentences.zh: 然而，在安全的环境里始终保持高度警惕，就会徒耗精力。

sentences.en: So, a neural switch that automatically increases or decreases our ability to process warnings in response to changes in our environment could have been useful.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种能随环境变化而自动增强或减弱我们处理警示信息能力的神经开关，过去也许很有用。

sentences.en: In fact, people with clinical depression and anxiety seem unable to switch away from a state in which they absorb all the negative messages around them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，临床抑郁和焦虑患者似乎无法摆脱这样一种状态，周围的负面信息他们全都会吸收。

sentences.en: It is also important to realise that stress travels rapidly from one person to the next.
sentences.zh: 还要认识到，压力会迅速从一个人传给另一个人。

sentences.en: If a co-worker is stressed, we are more likely to tense up and feel stressed ourselves.
sentences.zh: 如果同事压力很大，我们自己也更容易紧张起来，感到有压力。

sentences.en: We don’t even need to be in the same room with someone for their emotions to influence our behaviour.
sentences.zh: 即使不和对方待在同一个房间里，对方的情绪也能影响我们的行为。

sentences.en: Studies show that if we observe positive feeds on social media, such as images of a pink sunset, we are more likely to post uplifting messages ourselves.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，如果我们在社交媒体上看到积极的动态，比如一张粉红色晚霞的图片，我们自己也更可能发布振奋人心的消息。

sentences.en: If we observe negative posts, such as complaints about a long queue at the coffee shop, we will in turn create more negative posts.
sentences.zh: 如果看到负面帖子，比如有人抱怨咖啡店排队太长，我们也会转而发布更多负面帖子。

sentences.en: In some ways, many of us now live as if we are in danger, constantly ready to tackle demanding emails and text messages, and respond to news alerts and comments on social media.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，如今我们许多人的生活就仿佛身处危险中，时刻准备应付棘手的电子邮件和短信，回应新闻提醒和社交媒体上的评论。

sentences.en: Repeatedly checking your phone, according to a survey conducted by the American Psychological Association, is related to stress.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学会开展的一项调查表明，反复查看手机与压力有关。

sentences.en: In other words, a pre-programmed physiological reaction, which evolution has equipped us with to help us avoid famished predators, is now being triggered by an online post.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，进化赋予了我们一种预设的生理反应，好让我们避开饥肠辘辘的捕食者，如今一则网帖就能触发这种反应。

sentences.en: Social media posting, according to one study, raises your pulse, makes you sweat, and enlarges your pupils more than most daily activities.
sentences.zh: 一项研究发现，与大多数日常活动相比，在社交媒体上发帖，会让人的脉搏跳得更快、汗出得更多、瞳孔扩得更大。

sentences.en: The fact that stress increases the likelihood that we will focus more on alarming messages, together with the fact that it spreads extremely rapidly, can create collective fear that is not always justified.
sentences.zh: 压力使我们更可能把注意力放在令人不安的消息上，再加上压力本身传播极快，这两点可能引发并不总是有充分依据的集体恐惧。

sentences.en: After a stressful public event, such as a natural disaster or major financial crash, there is often a wave of alarming information in traditional and social media, which individuals become very aware of.
sentences.zh: 在令人紧张的公共事件之后，比如自然灾害或严重的金融崩盘，传统媒体和社交媒体上常会涌现大量令人不安的信息，人们会对这些信息格外留意。

sentences.en: But that has the effect of exaggerating existing danger.
sentences.zh: 但这会使原有的危险显得比实际更大。

sentences.en: And so, a reliable pattern emerges – stress is triggered, spreading from one person to the next, which temporarily enhances the likelihood that people will take in negative reports, which increases stress further.
sentences.zh: 于是，一种反复出现的模式就形成了。压力被激起，从一个人传给另一个人，这会让人们暂时更容易接收负面报道，从而进一步加重压力。

sentences.en: As a result, trips are cancelled, even if the disaster took place across the globe, stocks are sold, even when holding on is the best thing to do.
sentences.zh: 结果，即便灾难发生在地球的另一端，人们也会取消行程。即使继续持有才是最佳选择，人们也会抛售股票。

sentences.en: The good news, however, is that positive emotions, such as hope, are contagious too, and are powerful in inducing people to act to find solutions.
sentences.zh: 不过，好消息是，希望等积极情绪也能感染他人，而且能有力地促使人们采取行动，寻找解决办法。

sentences.en: Being aware of the close relationship between people’s emotional state and how they process information can help us frame our messages more effectively and become conscientious agents of change.
sentences.zh: 了解人的情绪状态和信息处理方式的密切联系，有助于我们更有效地组织措辞，成为尽责的变革推动者。
